prompt: A security review asks for the least-privilege default across dozens of repositories. What is the recommended posture?
explanation: Restrictive by default, expansive by exception: read-only tokens everywhere, and a `permissions:` block on the few jobs that write. A PAT in a secret is the anti-pattern — long-lived, broadly scoped, and copied into every run that reads it.

options.text: Keep broad read/write defaults for compatibility
Set default workflow permissions to read-only, granting writes job by job
Grant `write-all` on the workflows that need any write
Store a classic PAT with full repo scope as an organization secret
